title: Exploration of Berberine Against Ulcerative Colitis via TLR4/NF-kappaB/HIF-1alpha Pathway by Bioinformatics and Experimental Validation.
authors: Li, Jilei; Dan, Wenchao; Zhang, Chenchen; Liu, Nian; Wang, Yichong; Liu, Jixiang; Zhang, Shengsheng
one_liner_zh: 该文研究小檗碱通过TLR4/NF-kB/HIF-1α通路治疗溃疡性结肠炎，虽用分子对接和模拟，但对象为小分子-蛋白互作，非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，与本课题无关。
abstract: PURPOSE: This study aimed to delineate the molecular processes underlying the therapeutic effects of berberine on UC by employing network pharmacology tactics, molecular docking, and dynamic simulations supported by empirical validations both in vivo and in vitro. PATIENTS AND METHODS: We systematically screened potential targets and relevant pathways affected by berberine for UC treatment from comprehensive databases, including GeneCards, DisGeNET, and GEO. Molecular docking and simulation protocols were used to assess the interaction stability between berberine and its principal targets. The predictions were validated using both a DSS-induced UC mouse model and a lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-stimulated NCM460 cellular inflammation model. RESULTS: Network pharmacology analysis revealed the regulatory effect of the TLR4/NF-kappaB/HIF-1alpha pathway in the ameliorative action of berberine in UC. Docking and simulation studies predicted the high-affinity interactions of berberine with pivotal targets: TLR4, NF-kappaB, HIF-1alpha, and the HIF inhibitor KC7F2. Moreover, in vivo analyses demonstrated that berberine attenuates clinical severity, as reflected by decreased disease activity index (DAI) scores, reduced weight loss, and mitigated intestinal inflammation in DSS-challenged mice. These outcomes include suppression of the proinflammatory cytokines IL-6 and TNF-alpha and downregulation of TLR4/NF-kappaB/HIF-1alpha mRNA and protein levels. Correspondingly, in vitro findings indicate that berberine decreases cellular inflammatory injury and suppresses TLR4/NF-kappaB/HIF-1alpha signaling, with notable effectiveness similar to that of the HIF-1alpha inhibitor KC7F2. CONCLUSION: Through network pharmacology analysis and experimental substantiation, this study confirmed that berberine enhances UC treatment outcomes by inhibiting the TLR4/NF-kappaB/HIF-1alpha axis, thereby mitigating inflammatory reactions and improving colonic pathology.
abstract_zh: 目的：本研究旨在通过网络药理学策略、分子对接和动态模拟，并结合体内外实验验证，阐明小檗碱对溃疡性结肠炎（UC）治疗效果的分子机制。患者与方法：我们从综合数据库（包括GeneCards、DisGeNET和GEO）中系统筛选了小檗碱治疗UC的潜在靶点及相关通路。采用分子对接和模拟方案评估小檗碱与其主要靶点之间的相互作用稳定性。预测结果通过DSS诱导的UC小鼠模型和脂多糖（LPS）刺激的NCM460细胞炎症模型进行了验证。结果：网络药理学分析揭示了TLR4/NF-kappaB/HIF-1alpha通路在小檗碱改善UC中的调节作用。对接和模拟研究预测了小檗碱与关键靶点（TLR4、NF-kappaB、HIF-1alpha及HIF抑制剂KC7F2）的高亲和力相互作用。此外，体内分析表明，小檗碱可减轻临床严重程度，表现为DSS攻击小鼠的疾病活动指数（DAI）评分降低、体重减轻减少及肠道炎症缓解。这些结果包括抑制促炎细胞因子IL-6和TNF-alpha，以及下调TLR4/NF-kappaB/HIF-1alpha的mRNA和蛋白水平。相应地，体外研究结果表明，小檗碱可减少细胞炎症损伤并抑制TLR4/NF-kappaB/HIF-1alpha信号传导，其效果与HIF-1alpha抑制剂KC7F2相似且显著。结论：通过网络药理学分析和实验验证，本研究确认小檗碱通过抑制TLR4/NF-kappaB/HIF-1alpha轴来增强UC治疗效果，从而减轻炎症反应并改善结肠病理。
